predecessors.name: Turkestan ASSR
predecessors.text: Fergana and the countryside round Tashkent, held at the end of 1918

successors.name: Soviet Union
successors.text: East Bukhara and Fergana, reconquered by the Red Army by 1925 and mopped up to 1934

ledger.x: 1918: the Basmachi rebellion 'started in earnest' after the February assault on Kokand, under Irgash Bey, 'Supreme Leader of the Islamic Army'; its roots lay in the anti-conscription violence of 1916.
1918: by the end of the year 'decentralized bands of fighters, totaling roughly 20,000, controlled Ferghana and the countryside surrounding Tashkent'.
1920: the Tashkent countryside is lost to the Reds.
1921: the rebellion spreads to East Bukhara.
1925: Ibrahim Bek is beaten and East Bukhara lost.

wars.name: Basmachi revolt
wars.outcome: The Red Army defeated the Basmachi: Madamin Bey went over in 1920, Enver Pasha fell in August 1922, Ibrahim Bek was beaten in 1925 and executed in 1931.

certainty.note: Decentralized bands with no frontier; zones are approximate.
